title: Staged API evolution and LTS compatibility adviser
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Problem statement:
As the serving runtime evolves we need a repeatable, low-friction way to land changes that alter runtime behavior (APIs, request/response wire contracts, kernel selection signals, and plugin entrypoints) while limiting disruption to customers. Existing semver and LTS guidance is fragmented across docs. This ticket defines a single operational policy and builds the first iteration of a Compatibility Adviser that automates compatibility checks, produces deprecation manifests, and drives safe staged rollouts.

Goals (what success looks like):
- A clear, actionable runtime semantic versioning policy that classifies changes and prescribes public communication windows.
- LTS channel definitions and mapped deprecation windows for each change class.
- Automated tooling: a Compatibility Adviser service that generates a "compatibility score" for PRs and emits a deprecation manifest and migration hints.
- An Upgrade Assistant CLI that verifies client adapters and can apply opt-in codemod patches for common migration patterns.
- Rollout gate configuration defaults (canary %, monitoring duration, gating thresholds) and integration with existing release automation.

Scope / non-goals: 
- Scope includes API surface owned by the runtime process and public SDK contract points. It excludes internal admin tooling and one-off experimental feature flags.
- We are NOT changing the runtime API today; this ticket defines policy + tooling and implements adviser prototypes to validate flows.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc published and reviewed by Release Engineering, API, and Product teams.
Compatibility Adviser prototype runs on PRs and outputs a compatibility_score and a deprecation_manifest artifact.
Upgrade Assistant CLI can validate a downstream SDK repo against the deprecation_manifest and surface 5 example migration hints.
Default rollout gates defined and wired into canary orchestration; a dry-run canary executed in staging with monitoring reports.
End-to-end demo: merge a non-breaking minor change in staging; Adviser classifies as minor, rollout executes with default gates and shows no violations.
tasks: Write runtime semantic versioning policy draft (classification + deprecation windows + channel mapping).
Define LTS channels: Stable (18 months), LTS (36 months), Extended-LTS (optional, by contract).
Design compatibility_score algorithm (static AST checks + backward-compat telemetry delta weighting).
Implement Adviser prototype: GitHub PR bot that runs static checks and calls telemetry-based heuristics.
Create deprecation_manifest schema and storage (S3 + signed artifact).
Build Upgrade Assistant CLI prototype that ingests deprecation_manifest and runs compatibility checks against SDKs.
Define rollout gate defaults and thresholds and add them as runnable playbooks in release automation.
Run staged canary in preprod and capture metrics for gating thresholds.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha: Initial write-up and scope shared with release-eng and api-design. Requested input on LTS durations.
2026-03-04 - Marco: Proposed compatibility_score formula: 70% static compatibility, 30% runtime consumer telemetry. Asking infra for telemetry access window.
2026-03-07 - Priya (API): Raised concern about kernel selection signals being treated as breaking if they change default behavior; suggested separate 'behavioral' change class.
2026-03-10 - Security: Reviewed deprecation_manifest signing approach; recommend using KMS-signed artifacts. Marked security_review_required flag if manifest expands.
release_notes: Adds an operational semver policy and introduces prototype tooling to assist in safe rollouts and upgrades.
migration_plan_summary: Provide signed deprecation_manifests with every breaking or removal change. Upstream SDK owners run Upgrade Assistant which reports blocked APIs and can apply suggested codemods for trivial renames. Major and breaking changes must have an explicit migration guide and a 12-month deprecation window for general customers; critical security fixes may shorten this with notification.
